title: County buying private West Maui water systems
summary: At a September 30 special meeting, a council member said the County controls delivery of 23 percent of West Maui water and private companies deliver 77 percent, and that the Council recently approved buying three water systems. The County is still in due diligence on buying other systems, aiming for about 90 percent public control.

timeline.text: The member said the County is still in the due diligence (fact-checking) phase for buying other systems.
timeline.body: County Council Special Meeting

timeline.text: The county is still checking details on other water systems, aiming for about 90 percent public control.
timeline.body: County Council Special Meeting

timeline.text: A council member said the purchases will increase public control of water.
timeline.body: County Council Special Meeting

timeline.text: The member said the Council recently approved buying three water systems.
timeline.body: County Council Special Meeting

timeline.text: A council member said the County controls delivery of 23 percent of West Maui water, and private companies deliver 77 percent.
timeline.body: County Council Special Meeting

timeline.text: The water purchase passed 8–1, with the chair voting no.
timeline.body: County Council Meeting

timeline.text: A council member said the community on the West Side wants the County to buy the system.
timeline.body: County Council Meeting

timeline.text: The department said it created ten unfunded positions it plans to fill for the added work.
timeline.body: County Council Meeting

timeline.text: The chair said she had been told the department lacked enough staff to take over the system.
timeline.body: County Council Meeting

timeline.text: The department said a six-month due diligence period will show the total administrative costs to the County.
timeline.body: County Council Meeting

timeline.text: The water department said it will train and bring on extra employees during a transition of about six months.
timeline.body: County Council Meeting

timeline.text: He said funding for the purchase is already in the account.
timeline.body: County Council Meeting

timeline.text: The deputy water director said the deal includes wells, storage tanks, transmission lines, reservoirs and booster pumps.
timeline.body: County Council Meeting

timeline.text: The Council took up buying private water system assets for up to $6 million.
timeline.body: County Council Meeting

timeline.text: Item on the proposed acquisition of the irrigation company's water infrastructure assets: The chair deferred the item because the committee had to leave the room.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: Motion to enter executive session on DRIP 9.12, the proposed acquisition of an irrigation company's water infrastructure assets: The motion passed 7–0, with two members excused.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: The chair said this purchase covers the non-potable side, since the committee already voted on the potable side.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: The chair said the water resolution now goes on to the council chair.
timeline.body: County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee

timeline.text: The committee passed the water motion 7 to 1, with one member excused.
timeline.body: County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee

timeline.text: A member who supported the purchase said the West Side has been asking for public control over water.
timeline.body: County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee

timeline.text: Staff said yearly operating costs are about $879,000 for one system and $671,000 for the other.
timeline.body: County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee

timeline.text: An engineer said site walks found no leaks above normal.
timeline.body: County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee

timeline.text: No one signed up to testify on the water item.
timeline.body: County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee

timeline.text: The price would be up to $6 million, not counting closing costs.
timeline.body: County Council Budget, Finance, and Economic Development Committee

timeline.text: The managing director said these purchases, with others discussed this week, would raise public control of West Maui drinking water systems from about 45% to 93%.
timeline.body: County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: If the council acts in August, closing could come around April next year.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: Once the council approves, the County would start the Public Utilities Commission (PUC) process.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: After committee approval, the item would go to the full council for final approval.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: The administration plans to answer follow-up questions from committee staff, ideally by the August 4 meeting.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: The item is expected at Council Member Sugimura's committee on August 4.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: The chair said the item was for discussion only.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: Staff were asked to note a request to clarify when approval from a state water agency is needed.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: An official said only Public Utilities Commission (PUC) approval is needed for the purchase itself.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: The committee chair said the systems are in good shape and called the purchase a good deal for the community.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: A County attorney said they would check whether a right of first refusal is in the easement agreements.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: The department said the County will not buy the systems if the Public Utilities Commission (PUC) does not approve the sale.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: Officials said connecting the systems would give better resiliency and redundancy.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: The County would buy the companies' assets, not the companies themselves.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: Staff said they believe the County would get easements (rights to use land) for all assets, not the land itself.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: Another testifier supported the purchase but questioned paying above the appraised value for one system.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: A testifier said 77% of West Maui water systems are owned by private entities.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: Staff said they could try to separate the operating costs for one system's drinking and non-drinking water.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: Staff said the water tanks are in good condition and get yearly maintenance.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: The water department said the sellers would run the systems for about six months during the handover.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: Staff said the department needs Council approval to keep moving forward with the Public Utilities Commission (PUC) process.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: Staff said the County would buy only the systems' assets, not the companies, so it would not inherit company liabilities.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: The smaller system's price is $2.5 million, and it was appraised at $1.987 million.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: The larger system's price is $3.5 million, and it was appraised at $8,056,000.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: The larger system has three wells, two tanks and 402 active connections.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: The Director of Finance found the purchase is in the public interest to support long-term water service in West Maui.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee

timeline.text: The total price is up to $6 million, not counting closing costs.
timeline.body: County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee
